summary: Provisioning agent stalls when WSL2 vNIC appears before physical NIC (virtual NIC ordering)
description:
Issue summary:
Devices imaged from the developer workstation build that have WSL2 enabled are hanging during the provisioning agent startup phase. The agent attempts to bind to a network interface by ordinal index, but the presence of the WSL2 virtual NIC changes adapter ordering and the bind fails, leaving the agent in a StartPending/loop state and blocking downstream Intune/SCCM check-ins.

Impact:
- New developer laptops imaged from the dev image fail device check-in and policy application (approx 8 devices affected in last 48h).
- Onboarding is blocked for affected developers; MFA/profile provisioning doesn't complete.
- Manually disabling WSL2 or removing the vNIC allows provisioning to complete.

Environment:
- Corporate developer image (custom GoldenImage-Dev-2026-02)
- Windows 11 22H2 and 23H2 builds observed
- WSL2 optional feature enabled (Ubuntu 20.04 distro present on repro devices)
- Provisioning agent: redwood-provision-agent v1.4.2 (service name: RedwoodProvisionAgent)
- Intune + SCCM hybrid enrollment pipeline used during post-image provisioning
- Hardware: Dell Latitude 9440, Lenovo T14s repro devices

Steps to reproduce:
1) Apply GoldenImage-Dev-2026-02 to target machine (image includes WSL2 enabled).
2) Reboot and allow OOBE to reach provisioning stage.
3) Provisioning pipeline starts; redwood-provision-agent service attempts interface bind during startup.
4) Agent logs show bind failure and service enters repeated restart attempts.

Observed behavior:
- Provisioning agent log excerpt: "ERROR network: failed to bind adapter index 2: interface not found" followed by repeated "ServiceControl: start failed, retrying" messages.
- SCCM client does not complete initial check-in; Intune device record remains in 'Pending'.
- ProcMon capture shows creation of "vEthernet (WSL)" adapter before agent service start.

Expected behavior:
- Agent should identify and bind to the correct physical management NIC regardless of transient virtual adapter ordering, or fall back to a robust selection strategy (GUID/connection profile) instead of relying on ordinal index.

Logs / evidence:
- Attached: provisioning-agent.log (excerpt), System Event log entries around service start, ProcMon trace snippet (redacted), screenshots of network adapter list ordering.
- Related Confluence runbook: /confluence/runbooks/provisioning-agent-troubleshooting (see link in related_confluence_pages).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Maya Patel: Initial report after reproducing on two dev laptops. WSL2 appears to add vEthernet adapter ahead of physical NIC; provisioning agent bind-by-index fails.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Liam Nguyen: Captured ProcMon and agent logs. Preliminary hypothesis: agent uses GetAdaptersAddresses and assumes stable ordering; WSL vNIC insertion shifts indexes. Will try forcing agent to enumerate by IF_GUID.

2026-03-11 09:30 - SRE (Daniel Cho): Confirmed repro in lab. Temporary workaround: disable WSL optional feature in image build or schedule agent start after device network stabilization. Both are undesirable long-term fixes.

2026-03-12 14:20 - Eng (Sofia Martinez): Code change proposed to lookup adapter by connection profile (NdisPhysicalMedium / registry GUID) and to fall back to IP route-based selection. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provision-agent/pull/482
2026-03-12 16:45 - Liam Nguyen: Patch applied to staging images; rolling a validation batch of 12 devices. Monitoring for any side effects.
investigation_notes: ProcMon shows WSL vNIC creation occurs as part of feature initialization before the agent service start triggered by provisioning pipeline.
Agent code inspects adapter list and binds to the adapter at index N derived from image metadata (legacy behavior from earlier static images).
Devices with WSL disabled or with vNIC removed do not reproduce the failure. Devices with Hyper-V virtual adapters (other vSwitches) can also cause similar ordering shifts.
Reproduced on both physical hardware and Hyper-V nested VM with WSL feature toggled on/off.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigations: (1) Disable WSL feature in the GoldenImage used for onboarding; (2) Add a pre-provisioning step to delay agent start until network adapters settle (not ideal).

Permanent fix: Agent updated to select management NIC by persistent interface GUID or by evaluating the interface with default route and operational state. PR #482 implements GUID-first lookup with route-based fallback.
Patch merged to main on 2026-03-12; a hotfix build (v1.4.3) was published to the staging package feed and applied to GoldenImage-Dev-2026-02b for validation.
Follow-ups: add unit tests for adapter-order changes, add image pipeline check to detect presence of virtual adapters and surface a warning, update provisioning runbook to include WSL2 note.
Rollout plan: staged rollout to dev image fleet (100 devices) then to broader onboarding images pending 48h validation.
